== Description ==
The '''Bug''' was an [[Enemies|enemy]] that could only be found in the [[Hidden Wave (Legacy)|legacy Hidden Wave]], which meant it could only be found in [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode.

The '''Bug''' was extremely fast and had a very high amount of health. This enemy was extremely difficult to defeat without correct precautions and it could have easily made you lose the [[Hidden Wave (Legacy)|Hidden Wave]] without the right towers.

==Appearance==
The '''Bug''' had a very similar appearance to the [[Error]] and [[Glitch]], though more glitch particles were emitted from the '''Bug''' and it had an emblem of a bug on the front torso. While it was alive, the color of the '''Bug''' changed every second. It was also faceless. When it ran, a colorful glitch trail was left behind.

==Strategy==
*Do not underestimate the '''Bug''' as if it was a [[Glitch]] or an [[Error]] due to its high amount of health.
*Every tower must be maxed out and prepared for [[enemies]] like this in the [[Hidden Wave (Legacy)|Hidden Wave]], so it is recommended to bring certain towers in order to beat the wave.
**[[DJ Booth]]s and [[Commander]]s are needed for range and [[Firerate Buff]]s respectively.
** Level 5 [[Ranger]]s are also highly recommended to defeat this, though their firerates must be boosted due to the incredibly high speeds attained by the '''Bug'''. 
*The [[Electroshocker]] is quite useful against the '''Bug''' as it can slow hordes of them down for a long period of time.
**The [[Frost Blaster]] and [[Freezer]] can also be used, though they can only freeze '''Bugs''' one at a time.
**The [[Sledger]] can be used to freeze hordes of '''Bugs''' due to its piercing, though due to its slow swingrate, some '''Bugs''' may not be frozen at all.
** The [[Toxic Gunner]] can also be helpful, as it slows the '''Bug''' by up to 50%, though it may take a while to slow down a horde of '''Bugs'''.
**If you are using the [[Accelerator]], use the [[Freezer]] or [[Electroshocker]] to give time for the [[Accelerator]] to charge up.
